$comment: Catalog-level UI builder policy for :widget-catalog, the `remote-widgets` system: Mobile Launcher Widgets in Remote Compose. Modelled on remote-catalog/ui-builder.policy.json (`remote-m3`) and deliberately different from it in three places, each the reason this is a design system of its own: the vocabulary is remote-creation-compose + remote-foundation with no remote-material3 (so no theme roles, no type scale), the root is a launcher widget (an AppWidgetProvider, upstream's RemoteComposeWidget) rather than a Glance Wear container, and the frame sizes are launcher GRID CELLS rather than devices or Wear container sizes. Per-component policy stays on the stickers. See docs/design/REMOTE_WIDGETS_UI_BUILDER.md.

native.reason: The generated RemoteComposeWidget Kotlin, compiled against this module's own classpath (remote-creation-compose + remote-foundation, the vendored port) and rasterised by the real player under the WIDGETS_V6 profile a launcher widget records with.

$comment_previewSurfaces: No `wasm` surface yet. remote-m3's Visual Editor draws Wear Compose CMP stand-ins and its Browser Preview is a catalog-owned runtime (:remote-catalog-ui-builder-renderer); a launcher-widget runtime would reuse that renderer's foundation adapters and CMP writer/player pair but not its Wear and Material adapters, and is the next step rather than part of this initial system.

frame.$comment_adapter: A launcher widget is drawn into the rectangle the launcher gives it, measured in grid cells. `frame/launcher-widget`, not remote-m3's `frame/widget-host` (a Wear host container) nor a device frame.

geometry.$comment: The sizes are DISCRETE LAUNCHER GRID UNITS: each `label` is the cell count a design is authored at (`3x2`), and its dp the portrait size Android documents for that count, (73n - 16) x (118m - 16) dp (developer.android.com/develop/ui/views/appwidgets/layouts, measured on a Pixel 4's 5x4 grid). Real launchers vary the cell size, which is why the cell count is what a design states and this dp is its reference rendering. The same table is WidgetSize in widget-catalog/src/main/kotlin/ee/schimke/remotewidgets/WidgetSizes.kt and the breakpoints in catalog.spec.json; WidgetSizeTest holds all three together.

$comment_composeSourceExport: The Compose source emitter this catalog's designs export through (compose-ui-builder's CatalogExportRouting). `remote-compose-launcher-widget` writes a launcher widget at the cell sizes this catalog's frame declares; it is the emitter a `remote-widgets` design reaches today, and declaring it lets the catalog own its export.
$comment_colorTokens: No `colorTokens`. A colour role exports as `RemoteMaterialTheme.colorScheme.<role>`, which is remote-material3 — the library this system does not have. Every colour a design writes is a `#AARRGGBB` literal, exporting as `Color(0x…).rc`; the sheet's own palette is WidgetColors in WidgetComponents.kt.

menu.$comment: This catalog's @CatalogComponent(group = …) vocabulary. Widget leads because a design starts from the launcher widget root.

$comment_builtins: One: the launcher widget ROOT, which has no call site of its own for a record to find — it is the `Content(context, widgetId)` override of the generated RemoteComposeWidget, not a composable a body calls. Its size is the design environment's, picked from frame.geometry.sizesDp; its background is the widget's.

properties.name: background
properties.notes: The widget's background, filling the cell the launcher gives it: a `#AARRGGBB` literal, written as `RemoteModifier.background(Color(0x…).rc)` on the box `Content` draws. Unset leaves the widget transparent over the wallpaper. The corner radius is the launcher's: it clips every widget to its own `system_app_widget_background_radius`, so the root never authors one.

$comment_components: The sheet's own components and the creation DSL's text. Each `record` names the discovered call (module-relative FQN, the shape remote-m3 uses); the layouts (`layout/box`, `layout/row`, `layout/column`, …) need no entry, being the builder's generic Remote Compose vocabulary. A `canvasMapping` renames, for the editing canvas only, a name the Remote API spells differently from the canvas adapter it is drawn with (`fontSize` is `m3/text`'s `fontSizeSp`; `WidgetSurface`'s `content` is `layout/box`'s `children`), as remote-m3's do; it never changes the stored design or the export.

propertyCapabilities.name: text
propertyCapabilities.notes: The string the text draws, written as `"…".rs`.

propertyCapabilities.name: color
propertyCapabilities.notes: A `#AARRGGBB` literal, written as `Color(0x…).rc`. No theme roles: see $comment_colorTokens.

propertyCapabilities.name: maxLines
propertyCapabilities.notes: The most lines the text wraps to.

$comment_templates: Three starting points, all rooted on the launcher widget. The hello world is listed first. That is the chooser order once the catalog-owned cutover reads this list (UiBuilderNewDesignSeed.templateIds keeps the published order). It is not a declared default: the schema takes paths only and cannot mark one yet (SEED_TEMPLATES step 3), so which template opens selected is not this file's to say. It shows "Hello, World!" centred on the accent at 3x1 (203x102dp, the smallest grid size the line fits at 24sp), the same document compose-ui-builder's LauncherWidgetTemplates seeds; its generated Kotlin is the compiled golden generated/HelloWidget.kt. Then an empty 2x1 widget, and the 3x2 counter LAYOUT reproducing AndroidX's MyWidget demo — its row, its two WidgetButtons and its count. The template is the layout only and its buttons are inert: MyWidget's clicks are widget LAMBDA actions (`RemoteModifier.onClick { … }`, Kotlin run in the app's process), which a builder document cannot author, and WidgetButton takes no Remote action a design could bind instead. The working counter is CounterWidget.kt in this module. WidgetTemplateTest holds the templates to the grid table and to this policy's vocabulary; the generated Kotlin the counter becomes is the compiled golden generated/CounterWidget.kt.
